title: The Open Passage
premise: Quentin Delacroix, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane brothers' lending syndicate, salvages a chest from a flooded river bearing the seal of a nation that no longer exists. Inside are documents proving a wartime atrocity was ordered, not accidental—papers worth a fortune to the men who want them destroyed and priceless to the survivors seeking justice. Hunted upriver through monsoon season by debt collectors turned assassins, Quentin forms an uneasy alliance with Mara Ives, a ferry pilot whose brother's death is recorded in those very pages. In the end, Quentin must choose between selling the chest to clear his debts or delivering it to a tribunal that may hang him as an accomplice; he chooses truth, pays his debt in blood and honesty, and sails out of the delta with Mara as the floodwaters finally recede.
about_author: P. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former river pilot who spent a decade working the seasonal floods of Southeast Asia before turning to writing full-time. Known for weather-soaked adventure fiction, Galloway lives between boats and has never once been on time for anything.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A storm chase goes wrong on the Serevan River, wrecking his boat and deepening his debt to the Vane brothers. He salvages what he can, including a strange iron chest snagged in the flood debris. Emotional beat: desperation sharpened by curiosity—the first crack in his careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Optimists with Ledgers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The Vane brothers give him ten days to repay or forfeit everything, including his boat. Their cheerful menace establishes the stakes. That night he pries open the chest: sealed documents stamped with the defunct Republic of Kestrel's crest. Beat: dread mixed with the intoxicating sense that fate has dealt him a card.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Reading the waterlogged papers by lamplight, he realizes they document a massacre ordered by a general now celebrated as a national hero. He understands their value—and the danger. Beat: moral vertigo; he tries to convince himself to sell without reading further.

chapters.title: The Ferry Pilot
chapters.summary: Mara Ives's POV. Mara runs supplies through the flooded delta and recognizes Quentin's boat at a fuel dock. She offers passage upriver—for a price she doesn't yet name. Beat: wary mutual assessment; two people who trust no one recognizing something familiar in each other.

chapters.title: Ten Days
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. First Vane collector, Ossler, finds him at the dock, polite and terrifying. Quentin lies about the chest's contents while loading it onto Mara's ferry. Beat: the clock starts ticking; paranoia becomes a way of life.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rules
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the river, Mara teaches Quentin the unwritten laws of monsoon travel—who can be bribed, which checkpoints are fatal. She notices he sleeps holding the chest like a child. Beat: grudging respect forming under constant rain.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Kilometer Nine
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A bribed checkpoint officer tips off Ossler; Quentin barely smuggles the chest past a search by hiding it in a coffin bound for a riverside funeral. Beat: first real brush with violence, and the realization this is no longer about money.

chapters.title: The Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara glimpses a document listing officers present at the Kestrel massacre—and finds her brother's executioner's signature. She confronts Quentin, who admits what he's carrying. Beat: betrayal curdling into alliance; her price is now justice, not money.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The river rises faster than any season on record; they shelter in a drowned church with other stranded travelers, including a retired Kestrel archivist who confirms the documents are authentic—and explosive. Beat: brief community, fragile hope.

chapters.title: Ossler's Offer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Ossler corners Quentin alone: the Vanes will forgive the entire debt if he hands over the chest—or Mara dies if he doesn't. Beat: loyalty versus survival laid bare; Quentin lies to Ossler's face for the first time and feels himself change.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The old archivist reveals he helped bury the records decades ago and has waited for someone brave enough to surface them. He gives them a route to the international tribunal at Corvane—but warns the general's loyalists control the last stretch of river. Beat: purpose crystallizes into a plan.

chapters.title: Leaking
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The ferry takes shrapnel damage escaping a loyalist patrol boat; they run aground in mangrove shallows and patch the hull by firelight. Mara's fevered exhaustion forces Quentin to care for her. Beat: tenderness admitted at last, spoken only because they might not survive.

chapters.title: The General's Son
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They're captured by loyalists led by the general's son, Dain Vosk, who reads the documents and—shatteringly—already knew. He offers to let them go if they surrender the chest to be burned quietly. Beat: the enemy revealed as another prisoner of the lie.

chapters.title: Escape at Slack Tide
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin engineers an escape during a tidal lull, sabotaging the loyalists' boat but refusing to kill Dain when he has him at gunpoint. Beat: Quentin discovers he'd rather lose everything than become the thing he's running from.

chapters.title: What Debts Are For
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The second Vane brother, Callum, intercepts them personally—not for the chest anymore, but because Quentin's defiance threatens the syndicate's reputation. He offers Quentin a partnership instead of punishment. Beat: temptation at its most seductive; power dressed as friendship.

chapters.title: The Burned Village
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. They pass through a village erased from every map—the massacre site itself—where survivors still keep vigil. An old woman thanks Mara for carrying the names home. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve; the abstract becomes sacred.

chapters.title: Storm Front
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The season's worst storm bears down just as Ossler, Callum, and Dain converge on the final river bend. Three-way pursuit in whiteout rain. Beat: all threads tightening toward collision; no clean exits remain.

chapters.title: The Open Passage
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Climax begins: Quentin runs the lethal flood channel called the Open Passage—the one route no pilot survives—to shake the pursuers, with Mara navigating by memory and nerve. Beat: terror and exhilaration fused; love expressed as absolute trust.

chapters.title: Reckoning at Corvane
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They reach the tribunal docks half-drowned; Callum holds a gun on them as Quentin testifies. Ossler turns on Callum to save himself, and the syndicate devours its own. Beat: catharsis—truth spoken aloud at last, at gunpoint, and it holds.

chapters.title: Judgment
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The tribunal authenticates the documents; the general is posthumously indicted and living accomplices arrested—including, painfully, Quentin himself briefly detained for salvage theft. Mara testifies for him. Beat: justice outside the law proving imperfect but real; Quentin accepts consequence without flinching.

chapters.title: Settled Accounts
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Released with a warning, Quentin learns the Vanes have collapsed and his debt died with their ledger. He and Dain share a bitter, honest drink—two men freed by the same truth. Beat: quiet reckoning; debts paid in ways money never could.

chapters.title: Fair Winds, Small Debts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Epilogue: months later, Quentin and Mara pilot cargo upriver together, the chest donated to the Kestrel memorial archive. A new storm builds on the horizon and, for once, they sail toward it willingly. Beat: peace earned, love chosen over safety, the horizon open.
